study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Ge et al., Lancet Digital Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modelling of brain morphometry across the lifespan with CentileBrain: algorithm benchmarking and model optimisation

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study systematically compared 8 algorithms for normative modeling: OLSR, BLR, GAMLSS, LMS (subclass of GAMLSS), GPR, WBLR, HBR, and MFPR. MFPR emerged as the preferred algorithm due to combined advantages in accuracy and computational efficiency. The optimized models used MFPR with non-linear fractional polynomials of age and linear effects of global neuroimaging measures.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: The multivariate fractional polynomial regression (MFPR) emerged as the preferred algorithm, optimised with non-linear polynomials for age and linear effects of global measures as covariates. ... Across all sex-specific and region-specific models, the LMS, GPR, WBLR, and MFPR had comparable values for MAE, RMSE, and explained variance that were statistically better at PFDR<0.05 than those for GAMLSS, BLR, OLSR, and HBR. Accordingly, the MFPR emerged as the preferred algorithm given its combined advantages in accuracy and computational efficiency.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled 150 regional morphometry measures including: global measures (total intracranial volume, mean cortical thickness, total surface area), cortical thickness and cortical surface area from 68 Desikan-Killiany atlas regions, and 14 subcortical volumetric measures based on the Aseg atlas. Sex-specific normative models were developed separately for each measure.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Morphometric feature extraction from whole-brain T1-weighted images was implemented with the standard pipelines in the FreeSurfer image analysis suite (appendix 2) to yield global measures of total intracranial volume, mean cortical thickness, and total surface area, as well as measures of cortical thickness and cortical surface area from the 68 Desikan-Killiany atlas regions and 14 subcortical volumetric measures based on the Aseg atlas. Sex-specific normative models were developed separately for each of the 150 regional morphometry measures

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The optimal models included age (as non-linear fractional polynomials) and global neuroimaging measures as explanatory variables. For subcortical volume models: intracranial volume; for cortical thickness models: mean cortical thickness; for cortical surface area models: total cortical surface area. Sex was handled by creating separate sex-specific models rather than as a covariate. Scanner vendor, Euler's number, and FreeSurfer version were tested but had small effects and were not included in the final optimized models.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: The effect of the scanner, Euler's number (appendix 1 p 3), and FreeSurfer version on model performance was small, whereas the opposite was the case for the global neuroimaging measures. Therefore, optimised models included age and global neuroimaging measures (ie, intracranial volume, mean cortical thickness, or total cortical surface area, as indicated). ... we define the optimal models as the sex-specific and region-specific models that were based on the MFPR algorithm with non-linear fractional polynomials of age and linear effects of the appropriate global neuroimaging measure (ie, intracranial volume for models of regional subcortical volumes, mean cortical thickness for models of regional cortical thickness, and total cortical surface area for models of regional cortical surface area).
